translationRepairs: Day guimao: Xiao Chao, newly made minister of education and prince of Poyang, and Xiao Zilong, prince of Suizhou and central-army general-in-chief, were put to death.
Day guiwei: Xiao Chao, newly made minister of education and prince of Poyang, and Xiao Zilong, prince of Suizhou and central-army general-in-chief, were put to death.

Chinese day graph 癸未 is the sexagenary day guiwei; the original English guimao corresponds to 癸卯 and is a real naming error. The proposed replacement corrects only that day name and otherwise matches the Chinese.
Day guimao: the newly appointed Minister of Education Prince Chao of Poyang and Central-Army General-in-Chief Prince Zilong of Suizhou were executed.
Day guiwei: the newly appointed Minister of Education Prince Chao of Poyang and Central-Army General-in-Chief Prince Zilong of Suizhou were executed.
Chinese day graph 癸未 is guiwei, not guimao (癸卯); the literal field makes the same day-name error as the idiomatic, and the proposed fix restores the correct reading without other changes.
Also killed were Xiao Rui, prince of Nanping and inspector of Xiangzhou; Xiao Chao, prince of Jinxi and inspector of Ying; and Xiao Keng, prince of Yidu and inspector of South Yuzhou.
Also killed were Xiao Rui, prince of Nanping and inspector of Xiangzhou; Xiao Qiu, prince of Jinxi and inspector of Ying; and Xiao Keng, prince of Yidu and inspector of South Yuzhou.

Chinese 晉熙王銶 names Prince Qiu of Jinxi; 銶 is Qiu, while Chao belongs to 鏘 (鄱陽王鏘) in s0028. The original idiomatic wrongly transfers Chao onto this prince, and the proposed Xiao Qiu is the accurate given-name reading.
Also executed were Inspector of Xiangzhou Prince Rui of Nanping, Inspector of Yingzhou Prince Chao of Jinxi, and Inspector of South Yuzhou Prince Keng of Yidu.
Also executed were Inspector of Xiangzhou Prince Rui of Nanping, Inspector of Yingzhou Prince Qiu of Jinxi, and Inspector of South Yuzhou Prince Keng of Yidu.
Chinese 晉熙王銶 is Prince Qiu of Jinxi; the literal Prince Chao misreads 銶 as Chao (proper to 鏘). Replacing Chao with Qiu corrects the given name without altering the rest of the sentence.
